name: Washington County
tax_rate: 9% county (plus city rates of 2.5%-4% and the 1.5% state tax); Explore Tualatin Valley receives 2.33 points of the county 9% for its tourism fund
deadline_pattern: Foundation Award opens in July and closes mid to late September (Sept 15, 2025; Sept 30, 2026) with awards announced by December 15; Inspiration Event Award runs on separate rounds for summer and fall/winter events
annual_pool: Foundation Award: up to $75,000 per fiscal year, up to $20,000 per project; 2025 round awarded $52,500 to five nonprofits. Inspiration Event Award: up to $5,000 per event, $27,400 awarded for summer 2025 events and $16,500 for Oct 2025 to June 2026 events
contact: Explore Tualatin Valley (Washington County Visitors Association), engage@tualatinvalley.org, 503-644-5555 or 800-537-3149, 12725 SW Millikan Way, Suite 210, Beaverton, OR 97005; Dave Parulo, President and CEO
notes: Washington County itself runs no grant round; it contracts its TLT tourism share to Explore Tualatin Valley, which runs two competitive programs: the Foundation Award for tourism development projects (small capital, experiences, public art, trails, signage; marketing-only projects excluded) and the Inspiration Event Award for events, plus a tourism signage program. Nonprofits, tribes and government partners apply; applications go to the ETV Executive Committee and then the Board of Directors. Nothing found on how the county or ETV will respond to HB 4148 in 2027.

name: Baker County
tax_rate: 7% county (collected only outside Baker City since July 1, 2025, when Baker City began its own 7% city tax) plus 1.5% state; TLT Committee reviews the rate each October for January 1
deadline_pattern: Rolling: TLT Tourism Grant (events, up to $5,000) applications accepted 180 to 60 days before the event and presented at the next monthly TLT Committee meeting (third Thursday); Collaborative Marketing Support (up to $2,500) due 90 days before the event; Tourism Related Facility grants have no deadline; grant funds reset each July 1
typical_open: Fiscal year opens July 1; applications accepted year-round while funds last
annual_pool: Not published. County TLT was $954,000 in FY2024 (before Baker City withdrew); the county projected a $1.6M carryover in 2025 and paid Baker City $425,500 in start-up tourism funds in May 2025
contact: Jessica Hobson, Baker County Marketing Director (Travel Baker County), info@travelbakercounty.com, 541-519-0763, 490 Campbell Street, Baker City; applications to Shelly Christensen, Baker County Administrative Services, schristensen@bakercountyor.gov, 1995 Third Street, Baker City, 541-523-8209
notes: The county's Transient Lodging Tax Committee (chair Tyler Brown of Barley Brown's) recommends and the three commissioners approve three programs: event grants up to $5,000 for any individual, business or organization whose event boosts food, retail and lodging in Baker County; collaborative marketing support up to $2,500 for advertising only; and Tourism Related Facility grants for public or nonprofit facilities with a 10% match. Applicants present at the monthly committee meeting and must report within 60 to 90 days after the event. Since July 1, 2025 Baker City collects its own 7% tax and spends it through a city council process with its own TLT committee (Tyler Brown, Michael Wilson, Ryan Dooley, Alicia Bowers, Robin Nudd, appointed July 2025) and a $35,000 event grant line in its 2025-26 plan, so events inside city limits should also approach the city. County revenue is now far smaller than the $954,000 FY2024 figure. Ordinance 2025-05 (June 2025) formalized the county committee. Nothing found on HB 4148 positions.
members_source: https://bakercityherald.com/?p=227358 and https://www.bakercountyor.gov/pages/tlt/TLT_Facts_Sheet.pdf; full committee roster not published online

presentation.pattern: Applicant or representative presents the request at the next monthly TLT Committee meeting, typically the third Thursday; post-event results presented within 90 days
presentation.format: In-person presentation to the committee; facility applicants may be invited to an oral presentation

meeting_schedule: TLT Committee meets monthly, typically the third Thursday; Board of Commissioners gives final approval at a regular session
pool_note: County TLT was $954,000 in FY2024 with Baker City generating about 80%; the city withdrew July 1, 2025 so current county revenue is roughly a fifth of that plus a carryover projected at $1.6M in 2025. Contracts paid from TLT: Chamber visitor center $94,970, marketing director $70,000, economic development director $56,760. No grant budget line is published.

name: Baker City
tax_rate: 7% city (Ordinance 3410 adopted June 24, 2025; city collection began July 1, 2025, replacing county collection inside city limits; 5% operator allowance) plus 1.5% state
deadline_pattern: Program forming: the first-year tourism plan carries a $35,000 Event Grants line for new events that bring tourists to Baker City plus $35,000 special events marketing; a city lodging tax committee modeled on the county's reviews requests and recommends to council; application form and deadlines not yet published
annual_pool: City manager projected about $800,000 in year one (FY2025-26); 70% (about $560,000) to tourism, 30% (about $240,000) to city services (police, fire, a community development coordinator). First-year tourism plan of $570,500 included $35,000 event grants, $35,000 special events marketing, $120,000 wayfinding, $100,000 tourism facilities, $35,000 travel publication advertising and $25,000 each for collaboration, co-op and downtown marketing
contact: Karen Miller, Community Development Coordinator, City of Baker City (introduced the tourism RFP); Barry Murphy, City Manager; Baker City Hall 1655 First Street, Baker City, OR 97814
notes: Baker City withdrew from the 2006 county agreement and has collected its own 7% TLT since July 1, 2025, seeded with $425,500 of county carryover approved May 7, 2025. Council appointed a five-member city TLT committee on July 22, 2025 (Tyler Brown, Michael Wilson, Ryan Dooley, Alicia Bowers, Robin Nudd) and issued an RFP for a firm to build the city tourism marketing program (brand, research, social, website); the committee and council review proposals and funding requests. The adopted first-year plan has a $35,000 event grant line and $35,000 special events marketing, so a Baker City event should contact Karen Miller for the request process while formal guidelines are drafted. Baker City Downtown holds a separate $25,000 visitor services agreement. City-only revenue of about $800,000 is roughly four times what the county now collects outside the city.

notes: Talent replaced its old transient room tax with an 11% TLT in July 2025, extended it to Airbnb-type platforms and directed the state to collect, with collections starting about 90 days after the IGA. The ordinance sends 70% to tourism promotion and tourism-related facilities including park elements used for visitor events, but council has not created a grant process; a September 2025 request for $2,000 for the Talent Skate Classic was handled as an ad hoc agenda item with the Talent Business Alliance offered as a sponsorship pass-through. Talent also faces a structural budget gap (phased public engagement launched July 2025), so expect the 30% general share to be prioritized. Watch the FY2026-27 budget for a community tourism grant line.
